Vyshhorodok Old Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Ternopil Oblast, Ukraine

Not demolished. Vyshhorodok's Jewish population, 96.7 percent of the town by 1921 despite wartime decline, followed mainly Trysk Hasidism and was led in the 1920s-30s by Rabbi Meir Frenkel. On March 16, 1942, the town's Jews were confined to the Vyshnivets ghetto, documented elsewhere in this collection, and executed there during its liquidation on August 11, 1942 — the same date and site as Vyshnivets's own community. This is the older of Vyshhorodok's two Jewish cemeteries, existing by the first part of the 18th century.
